papers.title: AMPK: a master regulator of mitochondrial quality and quantity.
papers.did: Reviews how AMPK, an ancient energy-sensing kinase, controls mitochondrial fission, fusion, biogenesis, and mitophagy.
papers.found: AMPK drives fragmentation of the mitochondrial network by promoting fission and inhibiting fusion, increasing mitochondrial number while allowing isolation of dysfunctional fragments.
papers.used: Literature synthesis on AMPK signaling and mitochondrial biology.
papers.why: Proposes that mitochondrial quality control was an ancient, conserved function of AMPK, relevant to metabolic disease and aging.
papers.anchor_quote: It drives fragmentation of the network by promoting fission and inhibiting fusion, increasing mitochondrial number while allowing isolation of dysfunctional fragments from the network.

papers.title: HDAC Inhibition Sensitizes Pancreatic Tumors to DNA Damage by Global Redistribution of the Transcriptional Machinery
papers.did: Investigated how Class I HDACs regulate the DNA damage response in pancreatic cancer and developed a tumor-selective nanoparticle for HDAC inhibitor delivery.
papers.found: HDAC inhibition heightens DNA damage and sensitizes PDAC to diverse DNA-damaging agents; entinostat-loaded bottlebrush prodrug nanoparticles achieved tumor-selective HDAC inhibition with reduced systemic toxicity.
papers.used: Entinostat (HDAC1/2 inhibitor), bottlebrush prodrug nanoparticles, ChIP for H3K27ac/BRD4/Pol II occupancy at DDR genes.
papers.why: Offers a precision drug-delivery strategy to overcome the systemic toxicity that has limited clinical use of HDAC inhibitors in pancreatic cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: HDAC inhibition by entinostat shifts the balance of H3K27 acetylation preferentially towards intergenic regions, diverting BRD4 and Pol II from promoters, thereby suppressing DDR gene expression.

papers.title: Med14 phosphorylation shapes genomic response to GLP-1 agonists.
papers.did: Used a proteomic screen to identify Med14, a Mediator complex subunit, as a mediator of chronic GLP-1 receptor agonist effects on pancreatic beta cells.
papers.found: Exendin-4 stimulates sustained Med14 phosphorylation at Ser983; mutating this site blocked Exendin-4's gene-regulatory effects and produced higher alpha-to-beta cell ratios.
papers.used: Proteomic screening, Ser983-mutant primary mouse islets, GLP-1 receptor agonists (Exendin-4).
papers.why: Reveals a molecular mechanism by which GLP-1 drugs reshape beta cell gene expression, relevant to diabetes treatment.
papers.anchor_quote: Exposure to Exendin-4 and other GLP-1 receptor agonists stimulates sustained phosphorylation of Med14 at Ser983, which corresponds to a conserved PKA recognition site.

papers.title: Synthesis and Characterization of ULK1/2 Kinase Inhibitors That Inhibit Autophagy and Upregulate Expression of Major Histocompatibility Complex I for the Treatment of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.did: Designed, synthesized, and characterized two new dual ULK1/2 kinase inhibitors for non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.found: Both compounds are cytotoxic against NSCLC cells and inhibit autophagic flux; one increases MHC class I expression, which may help overcome immunotherapy resistance.
papers.used: Medicinal chemistry synthesis, autophagic flux assays in A549 cells, MHC class I expression analysis.
papers.why: Supports ULK1/2 inhibitors as a cancer treatment strategy, alone or combined with immunotherapy.
papers.anchor_quote: SBP-5147 effectively modulates autophagy and increases the expression of major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class I in NSCLC cells, which may support the rationale for ULK1/2 inhibition as a strategy to overcome resistance to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Modeling lipid homeostasis using stable isotope tracing and flux analysis.
papers.did: Applied stable isotope tracing, mass spectrometry, and isotopologue modeling (Lipid-MFA) to measure lipid metabolic fluxes in lung cancer models.
papers.found: Found decreased fatty acid synthase and VLCFA elongation fluxes with increased sphingolipid recycling in p53-deficient versus LKB1-deficient NSCLC tumors.
papers.used: Stable isotope tracing, liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry, precision-cut lung slice culture.
papers.why: Provides a quantitative tool for studying lipid metabolism dysregulation across disease states.
papers.anchor_quote: Using Lipid-MFA, we observed decreased fatty acid synthase and very long-chain fatty acid (VLCFA) elongation fluxes, along with increased sphingolipid recycling, in p53-deficient versus liver kinase B1 (LKB1)-deficient NSCLC tumors using precision-cut lung slice culture.

papers.title: The AMPK Pathway: Molecular Rejuvenation of Metabolism and Mitochondria.
papers.did: Reviews advances in how AMPK modulates core mitochondrial life-cycle processes and restores mitochondrial health.
papers.found: AMPK homologs are found across all eukaryotic species and act as an ancient sensor of low cellular energy.
papers.used: Literature review of AMPK signaling across eukaryotic species.
papers.why: Frames AMPK as a central, evolutionarily conserved regulator linking energy stress sensing to mitochondrial rejuvenation.
papers.anchor_quote: Homologs of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) are found in all eukaryotic species and serve as an ancient sensor of conditions of low cellular energy.

papers.title: Leveraging autophagy and pyrimidine metabolism to target pancreatic cancer
papers.did: Studied pancreatic cancer cells with acquired resistance to autophagy inhibitors to uncover the metabolic adaptations that bypass autophagy inhibition.
papers.found: Resistant cells preferentially salvage pyrimidines instead of synthesizing them de novo, increasing sensitivity to pyrimidine analogues like gemcitabine.
papers.used: PDA cell lines with acquired resistance to autophagy inhibitors, metabolic profiling of TCA intermediates and nucleotide pools.
papers.why: Identifies a metabolic vulnerability that can be exploited with combination therapy for pancreatic cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: Cells adapting to loss of autophagy preferentially salvage pyrimidines to replenish these pools instead of synthesizing them de novo.

papers.title: Med14 phosphorylation shapes genomic response to GLP-1 Agonist
papers.did: Performed a proteomic screen to identify Med14 as a Mediator complex subunit mediating long-term GLP-1 analog effects on pancreatic beta cells.
papers.found: PKA-mediated phosphorylation of Med14 at Ser983 is essential for maintaining enhancers that drive beta cell-specific gene induction; mutating this site decreased beta cell numbers.
papers.used: Proteomic screening, primary mouse beta cells, Exendin-4 treatment.
papers.why: Explains the molecular basis for the long-term beneficial effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on beta cell function, relevant to diabetes therapy.
papers.anchor_quote: Phosphorylation of Med14 by PKA is essential for maintenance of enhancers that drive induction of beta cell-specific and diabetes-linked genes.

papers.title: FAM43A coordinates mtDNA replication and mitochondrial biogenesis in response to mtDNA depletion.
papers.did: Used mtDNA-depleted IMR90 cells as a model system to identify FAM43A as an early responder to mitochondrial DNA depletion.
papers.found: Depletion of FAM43A activates a mitochondrial biogenesis program, increasing mitochondrial mass and mtDNA copy number via CHK2-mediated upregulation of p53R2.
papers.used: mtDNA-depleted IMR90 cell model, CHK2-dependent signaling analysis.
papers.why: Reveals a checkpoint-like mechanism limiting mitochondrial biogenesis, relevant to human intergenomic signaling and mitochondrial disease.
papers.anchor_quote: We identified FAM43A, a largely uncharacterized protein, as a CHK2-dependent early responder to mtDNA depletion.

papers.title: Transcriptional repression by HDAC3 mediates T cell exclusion from Kras mutant lung tumors.
papers.did: Used genetic and pharmacological HDAC3 inhibition and mouse models to study HDAC3's role in the immune microenvironment of Kras-mutant lung tumors.
papers.found: HDAC3 inhibition combined with trametinib enhanced T cell recruitment into lung tumors, and T cells were shown to contribute to tumor growth control under this combination treatment.
papers.used: Genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs), genetic/pharmacological HDAC3 inhibition, entinostat plus trametinib combination treatment.
papers.why: Identifies HDAC3 as a druggable target to overcome T cell exclusion and improve immunotherapy response in Kras-mutant lung cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: Finally, we showed that T cells contribute to in vivo tumor growth control in the presence of entinostat and trametinib combination treatment.

papers.title: Modeling compound lipid homeostasis using stable isotope tracing
papers.did: Applied stable isotope tracing, mass spectrometry, and isotopologue modeling (CL-MFA) to quantify compound lipid metabolic fluxes in lung cancer models.
papers.found: Resolved LKB1-mediated regulation of sphingolipid recycling and identified previously uncharacterized isozyme specificity of ceramide synthase inhibitors.
papers.used: Stable isotope tracing, liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry, precision-cut lung slice cultures.
papers.why: Provides a tool (CL-MFA) to discover biological function and mechanisms in membrane lipid metabolism relevant to cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: Here, we resolve liver kinase B1 (LKB1)-mediated regulation of sphingolipid recycling in NSCLC cells and precision-cut lung slice cultures.

papers.title: EGFR-driven lung adenocarcinomas coopt alveolar macrophage metabolism and function to support EGFR signaling and growth.
papers.did: Investigated how EGFR-driven lung adenocarcinoma cells reprogram tumor-associated alveolar macrophages via GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling.
papers.found: Blocking PPARγ in tumor-associated alveolar macrophages combined with statin therapy further suppressed tumor progression and increased proinflammatory immune responses.
papers.used: Mouse models of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma, GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling analysis, statin combination therapy.
papers.why: Reveals new therapeutic combinations for immunotherapy-resistant EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.anchor_quote: In the absence of TA-AM metabolic support, LUAD cells compensate by increasing cholesterol synthesis, and blocking PPARγ in TA-AMs simultaneous with statin therapy further suppresses tumor progression and increases proinflammatory immune responses.

papers.title: Metabolic orchestration of cell death by AMPK-mediated phosphorylation of RIPK1.
papers.did: Investigated how AMPK regulates RIPK1-mediated cell death under metabolic stress using genetic mouse models.
papers.found: AMPK inhibits RIPK1 by phosphorylation at Ser415 to suppress energy stress-induced cell death; RIPK1 inactivation protected against ischemic injury in AMPK-deficient mice.
papers.used: TRAIL receptor signaling analysis, Ampk-deficient and RIPK1 S415A mutant mice, ischemic injury model.
papers.why: Reveals a crucial metabolic checkpoint integrating metabolism, cell death, and inflammation, with implications for treating ischemic injury.
papers.anchor_quote: AMPK inhibited RIPK1 by phosphorylation at Ser 415 to suppress energy stress-induced cell death.

papers.title: Inter-organelle cross-talk supports acetyl-coenzyme A homeostasis and lipogenesis under metabolic stress.
papers.did: Used 13C isotope tracing in cell lines deficient in mitochondrial (ACLY), cytosolic (ACSS2), and peroxisomal (PEX5) acetyl-CoA pathways to study acetyl-CoA homeostasis.
papers.found: Peroxisomal oxidation of exogenous lipids is a major source of acetyl-CoA for lipogenesis and histone acetylation in cells lacking ACLY.
papers.used: 13C isotope tracing, ACLY/ACSS2/PEX5 knockout cell lines, metabolic tracing.
papers.why: Highlights inter-organelle metabolic cross-talk as a mechanism supporting cell survival under nutrient fluctuation, relevant to cancer metabolism.
papers.anchor_quote: Metabolic tracing and PEX5 knockout studies link peroxisomal oxidation of exogenous lipids as a major source of acetyl-CoA for lipogenesis and histone acetylation in cells lacking ACLY, highlighting a role for inter-organelle cross-talk in supporting cell survival in response to nutrient fluctuations.

papers.title: Induction of lysosomal and mitochondrial biogenesis by AMPK phosphorylation of FNIP1.
papers.did: Demonstrated that AMPK directly phosphorylates five conserved serine residues in FNIP1 in response to mitochondrial damage.
papers.found: FNIP1 phosphorylation is required for AMPK to induce nuclear translocation of TFEB and TFEB-dependent increases of PGC1α and ERRα mRNAs.
papers.used: AMPK phosphorylation assays, FNIP1-FLCN complex analysis, TFEB nuclear translocation studies.
papers.why: Reveals how mitochondrial damage triggers sequential waves of lysosomal and mitochondrial biogenesis via the AMPK-FNIP1-TFEB axis.
papers.anchor_quote: We demonstrate that AMPK directly phosphorylates five conserved serine residues in folliculin-interacting protein 1 (FNIP1), suppressing the function of the folliculin (FLCN)-FNIP1 complex.

papers.title: EGFR+ lung adenocarcinomas coopt alveolar macrophage metabolism and function to support EGFR signaling and growth
papers.did: Investigated mechanisms by which EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma cells reprogram tumor-associated alveolar macrophages via GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling.
papers.found: Increased GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling drives tumor-associated alveolar macrophage properties, and blocking this axis suppresses cholesterol efflux to tumor cells and impairs EGFR phosphorylation.
papers.used: Mouse models of EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma, GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling analysis, statin combination therapy.
papers.why: Identifies GM-CSF-PPARγ signaling as a therapeutic target to restore immunotherapy sensitivity in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.anchor_quote: TA-AM properties are driven by increased GM-CSF—PPARγ signaling and inhibition of airway GM-CSF or PPARγ in TA-AMs suppresses cholesterol efflux to tumor cells, which impairs EGFR phosphorylation and restrains LUAD progression.

papers.title: HDAC3 is critical in tumor development and therapeutic resistance in Kras-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.did: Used genetically engineered mouse models to determine the in vivo role of HDAC3 in Kras-mutant lung cancer and its interaction with a MEK inhibitor.
papers.found: HDAC3 is required for lung tumor growth, directs FGFR1 expression via NKX2-1, and combining the HDAC1/3 inhibitor entinostat with trametinib produced therapeutic benefit in Kras/LKB1-mutant tumors.
papers.used: Genetically engineered mouse models (GEMMs), transcriptomics, entinostat/trametinib combination treatment.
papers.why: Establishes HDAC3 as a therapeutic target and identifies a combination therapy that overcomes trametinib resistance in Kras-mutant lung cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: We found that the combination of entinostat plus trametinib treatment elicits therapeutic benefit in the Kras/LKB1 GEMM.

papers.title: LKB1-Dependent Regulation of TPI1 Creates a Divergent Metabolic Liability between Human and Mouse Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.did: Used phosphoproteomics and metabolomics in human and mouse engineered cell lines and mouse models to compare TPI1 regulation between species.
papers.found: In human LUAD, TPI1 activity is regulated by SIK-mediated phosphorylation at Ser21 in an LKB1-dependent manner, while in mice this residue is instead regulated by oxidation, independent of LKB1.
papers.used: Phosphoproteomics, metabolomics, genetically engineered human cell lines and mouse models (GEMM).
papers.why: Explains a species-specific metabolic liability from LKB1 loss, cautioning about the limits of mouse models for studying human lung cancer.
papers.anchor_quote: In hLUAD, TPI1 activity is regulated via phosphorylation at Ser21 by the salt inducible kinases (SIK) in an LKB1-dependent manner, modulating flux between the completion of glycolysis and production of glycerol lipids.
